translation:
The heart is the sovereign fire, matching the five agents; venerating the sovereign in the Li position (south), water is born with it. The auxiliary wing, dragon-fire, is named minister fire; the thief of the primordial qi, truly hateful.
Taking advantage of opportunity it fans calamity, easily forgets to be moved (impulsive); bullying water it torments and boils, contending with the mingmen. For sthenia (replete) fire one drains with Daochi San (Drain-the-Red Powder); for deficiency fire one should supplement with Chaihenwan (Pull-the-Firewood Pill).
For the fire-pathogen of the individual channels, recognize the pulse and signs; from the clear decoction and cooling beverage subtract and increase. There is moreover the condition of yin deficiency with fire stirring; with Dihuang Liuwei (Six-Flavor Rehmannia), each essence-qi is replenished.
Daochi San within, three kinds of medicinals: Shengdi (Rehmannia) and Mutong (Akebia) gathered in one spot. Gancao (Licorice) tail-tip serving as deputy envoy; the startled heart with replete fire relaxes in an instant.
Qingliang Tang (Clear-Cool Decoction) uses Shengdihuang (Rehmannia); Zhizi (Gardenia), Xuanshen (Scrophularia), Lianqiao and Maimen (Ophiopogon). Gancao (Licorice), Jiegeng (Platycodon), Huanglian (Coptis) entering; a cup of water to quell the source of the ailment.

Chaihenwan (Pull-the-Firewood Pill)
Huanglian (Coptis), Huangbai (Phellodendron), Huangqin (Scutellaria), Zhizi (Gardenia), Mutong (Akebia), Xijiao (Rhinoceros horn/water buffalo horn), Shengdi (Rehmannia), Gancao (Licorice), Renshen (Ginseng), Wuwei (Schisandra), Maidong (Ophiopogon), Chaihu (Bupleurum).

Now the heart and small intestine are mutually exterior-interior; therefore when the heart is hot the small intestine is also hot, and urination must be red — this formula is for it. Shengdi can cool the heart blood. Gancao tip can drain the heat toxin, and assisted by Mutong it goes straight to the small intestine and bladder. Named Daochi San (Drain-the-Red); it is draining the bing-ding fire pathogen, discharging it by the urination.
translator_notes: 導赤散=Daochi San; 撤薪丸=Chaihenwan (Pull-the-Firewood, removing the firewood under the pot).
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Interior injury and exterior contraction must be distinguished; in the pulse distinguish the mouth-qi (qikou) from the ren-ying (carotid, at the neck). Exterior contraction of wind-cold is an excess (replete) condition; the back of the hand hot and nasal breath rapid.
Cold and heat erupt together without interval; the speech heavy-laden and heavy afterwards but light at first. Aversion to wind — to all wind it is feared; aversion to cold — facing the fire yet like ice.
Interior injury from eating and drinking is a deficiency; the palms of the hands blazingly hot, bitterly dizzy-headed. Cold and heat alternating, the mouth without flavor; the speech languid, lisping, the voice short.
Though there be a little (wind-cold), also one does not fear it; with the least warmth there is then no cold. One must know the deficiency within deficiency; Buzhong Yiqi (Supplement-the-Centre and Benefit-Qi) is marvelous as a spirit.
Buzhong Yiqi relies on Shen (Renshen/Ginseng) and Qi (Huangqi/Astragalus); Baizhu (Atractylodes), Gancao (Licorice), Dang Gui and Chenpi (Tangerine Peel). Chaihu (Bupleurum) turning to the left, Shengma (Cimicifuga) to the right; interior injury and exterior contraction both suit it.

The middle-spleen (zhong) is also the Kun (earth, the receptive); it is the mother of the ten-thousand things. Qi is yang, Qian (heaven, the creative); it is the father of ten-thousand things. Passing beyond exhaustion, toil and drudgery, then the hundred limbs all become deficient. It must steal from the parents to obtain nourishment, and the middle qi is greatly wounded. Without supplementing it, would not the form and qi nearly be severed? Therefore use the level supplementary Baizhu and Gancao to supplement the middle; use the vigorous supplementary Renshen and Huangqi to benefit the qi. Earth desiring dryness, then Dang Gui follows to moisten it; the qi desiring stagnation, then Chenpi follows to free it. And Shengma and Chaihu are what raise the qi of the jia-dan (gallbladder) and yi-gan (liver). For jia and yi are the beginning of living things in the east; when the qi of jia and yi ascends, then earth, fire, wood, metal and water must be born in order one after another.
translator_notes: 補中益氣湯=Buzhong Yiqi Tang (Supplement-the-Centre and Benefit-Qi Decoction).
氣口/人迎=qikou (wrist pulse) vs renying (carotid).
甲膽乙肝=the jia-gallbladder and yi-liver pairing.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Damp-heat toxic like (the toxin of) wine and its like; injected into the spleen and stomach, illness frequently present. Accumulated pain, coma, vomiting at frequent intervals; eating and drinking in small amounts is the spleen family's blame.
The method of treatment: sweat it and free the urine, above and below divide and clarify its dampness — wonderful. Gehua Jiexing Tang (Kudzu-Flower Relieve-Inebriation Decoction) does not change; all people are drunk but I alone am sober.
Gehua Jiexing (Kudzu-Flower Relieving-inebriation) with Renshen (Ginseng) and Ganjiang (Dried Ginger); Fuling (Poria), Zexie (Alisma), Zhu (Atractylodes) and Muxiang (Aucklandia). Qing (Qingpi) and Chenpi with Sharen (Amomum) and Shenqu (Medicated Leaven); with Doukou (Nutmeg/Cardamom) add to treat wine-damage.

Now the cold of Gehua (Kudzu Flower) can resolve the toxin within wine; the paleness of Fuling and Zexie can drain the dampness within wine. The pungency of Sharen, Doukou, Muxiang and Shengpi moves the stagnation of wine and food. Ganjiang is that which opens the stomach and stops vomiting; Shenqu is that which digests and grinds down roasted and greasy things. And the sweetness of Renshen and Baizhu is that which supplements and benefits the wounded spleen and stomach.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
